finding: the round-167 cost model underestimates GENERATION cost for cells whose dominating predecessors are not yet certified
cause: the (p) justification bound ub() is the minimum capacity over CERTIFIED cells that dominate the state componentwise.  The round-152 search had all 1,101 tabulated cells available; round 168 has only the 75 cells carried by verified exhaustion certificates, and none of them has d >= 14, so ub() falls back to the analytic 120 and the pruning collapses.

second_observation.status: stopped after about 4.6 hours and 4.6 GB of resident memory without finishing the maximisation
second_observation.action: deferred, not refuted -- a node cap is not an UNSAT

consequence_for_round_166_167: round 166 concluded that the certificate-order PREFIX is not required, and round 167 built the generation order on the round-152 node counts.  Both conclusions were measured on cells whose dominators happened to be certified already.  For a cell with no certified dominator the prefix is NOT free: it is the difference between 3.2 million and 256 million proof nodes.
not_a_soundness_problem: a missing predecessor only weakens pruning.  Every tree that IS produced is still a complete case analysis and is still independently replayed; the cost model is what was wrong, not the certificates.
round_169_implication: the generation order has to be chosen on the cost of generation under the CURRENT certified set, not on historical search nodes, and it has to account for a cell becoming cheap once a dominating cell is certified.  That is a scheduling problem round 167 did not solve because it did not know this effect existed.
